reviews.text: I loved everything. Not only the facilities, but also how well-prepared the place is, the very friendly staff, and the highly trained professionals. Without a doubt, a trustworthy clinic, not only for their expertise but also for their prices and their genuine love for animals. 100% recommended. I continue to have wonderful experiences with the care of my pets; they are so careful, professional, and loving with our animals. I especially want to thank Andrea for caring for one of my rescued angels. They are all incredible. And I will never stop thanking them for saving the lives of my Sheldon and Penny, and for taking Monana to heaven.

Does it seem logical to charge €80 for an animal that died during the consultation? How outrageous!

I went with my hamster, who was very sick. The vet examined her and gave me a quote of €370, including tests, X-rays, ultrasound, and blood work. I was shocked by those costs and told her no, I couldn't afford that. Then she quoted me €106 with medication and sent me home. When she handed her back to me, she said she could die at any moment. She tried to give her medication in front of me, but my hamster didn't respond. She said, "She looks very sick; she could die at any moment." And that's exactly what happened. She died in my hand inside the consultation room! I left with my little pet dead, and on top of that, I paid for nothing.

We took Leo there because he wasn't feeling well and we were worried. All the staff were very attentive from the moment we arrived. They treated him with great care and kept us informed at all times. A very positive experience.

I'm delighted with my experience at this clinic. From the very first moment, the entire team has been friendly, kind, and incredibly professional. It's clear they genuinely care about the animals and want both them and their families to feel comfortable and well taken care of.

I especially appreciated the way they patiently and clearly explained everything, answering all my questions and instilling a great deal of confidence.

Without a doubt, this is a clinic where I would leave my pet with complete peace of mind. Thank you so much to the whole team for your kindness, dedication, and professionalism! 🐾❤️

Hello. We regret that you had that perception about our prices.

However, we are surprised that we cannot find anyone with this information in our customer database, making it impossible for us to investigate what happened or which specific service the review refers to.

We would appreciate it if you could provide more information and details about your experience. This will not only allow us to verify what happened and give you an appropriate response, but also so that other people who read this review can understand the full context. Unfortunately, sometimes reviews appear that do not correspond to real experiences, and that is why we believe it is important to be able to identify and evaluate each case.

Regarding our prices, we are a veterinary hospital specializing in exotic animals with 24-hour service, and, for example, a veterinary consultation costs €35. We also maintain various charitable projects and collaborations with animal shelters and associations where many of our services are provided free of charge.

Therefore, we are particularly surprised by a review that only indicates "excessive price" without providing any other details about the service received.

We'd be happy to review your case if you provide us with more information.

They have no compassion. They told me my parrot was dying a month ago because I went to another vet who gave her medication. Because of them, my parrot no longer speaks when I go in just for a nail trim. They tricked us by saying they needed to do an x-ray and blood work. Very poor practice. Another thing: when my mother went to make an appointment, they told her she was the one who had to choose the day. Shameless. Because of them, my parrot is dying. I have to euthanize my parrot because they sent her home without medication. My parrot has already died. And I've taken care of her all the years I've had her. She wasn't weak, because in the taxi the parrot was talking, and she came out speechless and in very bad shape. And the vet was completely insensitive. 😡😡😡 I take much better care of my animals than I do of myself.
Thanks Mario

It's a pleasure to ask any questions, because Viki gives you all kinds of explanations and solutions to any doubt you might have.

I love that store. Thanks, Viki, I've finally found a place where they treat me very well and go out of their way to find solutions to any problem I have. I recommend it 100%.
Charming and very good professionals.
Thanks Edgar

It was my first time going to this vet with my dear friend Juan Alberto. My bearded dragon had been abandoned, and the first vet I saw didn't convince me, so I ended up coming here. Alba saw me, and judging by how young she is, she hasn't been here long. If that's the case, I have to say she's a fantastic find. She's very polite and empathetic; you can tell she loves animals. She was a great help, informing me about how to improve her care, since this is my first bearded dragon, and I asked her for advice. She cares deeply and remembers both the patient and their owners. She's attentive and gentle. She'll be my go-to vet. Thank you.

Edit two years later.

Honestly, it's become much more expensive (I'm not accusing them of trying to rip you off), and for me, the only vets worth it are Pablo and Patri. I haven't tried any others because on Monday the 31st, I took my pigeon to another vet with two broken legs, and well... she left the area around the toes unbandaged on one of the legs, and on the 2nd, I saw that it was super swollen and purple. Look, we're all human. We make mistakes, but today, because of that mistake, I had to spend another 12 euros on medication for circulation, which, well, might come in handy in the future. And on top of that, they charged me for a new bandage with the excuse that the animal could move around and tighten it itself... I've seen cases where the bandage loosens from movement... And besides, with both legs broken, it's not like it moves its legs much. She just wiggles around to adjust her position... And in the few days she went from having a more or less okay leg to being swollen and red... That doesn't make me think she did it herself... I really should have taken a "before" picture so you could see her leg, but in my naiveté, I thought that since it was a badly applied bandage, at least I wouldn't have to pay the price. By the way, the vet who told me that work has to be paid for... I work in a supermarket. At the checkout, if I accidentally break a product, we don't make the customer pay for it again... And I thought it was quite rude of him to say, "We do so much for pigeons by giving free consultations," as if it cost him anything or he lost something because of it... In that respect, only the owners lose out... In short, I'll probably change vets because, honestly, every time I try to go to a different one, I have problems. And I repeat. We're all human and we make mistakes, and if I have to buy more medication, I will. What bothered me was having to pay for a mistake made by the vet who treated Josefa, and frankly, the vet who saw me today was incredibly egotistical. I didn't react in the best way, but I didn't say anything offensive; I was simply stunned. It's a shame everything has changed so much...

I haven't been there much lately, but I'm very satisfied. I took two pigeons and a fish, a corydora, I think that's how it's spelled.

It tilts when it swims, and honestly... I didn't expect the vet to put so much effort into it, taking the time to examine it and find a solution, since the main problem is the fish's size. Besides, the consultation seemed quite inexpensive. It's more expensive elsewhere, and I'm really happy with the vet. If I remember correctly, I think his name was Miguel... THANK YOU SO MUCH!!!

We took our rat, Tofu Vicente, to the vet because of his aggressive behavior towards his four companions. We were very worried about his sudden change in attitude. The vet, who was very kind, explained a little about what was behind his behavior and suggested something simple that has been miraculous for us. Tofu won't have to live alone anymore, at least for now, an idea we were already resigning ourselves to. He's getting along wonderfully with everyone again, even better than before. We were very worried, but we've overcome another hurdle, and for now, that's enough. Thank you for your care!
Thank you, Alejandro.
I love the work Diana does and how she treats my pets; the attention she gives me every time I go is a real pleasure to be attended to by such a professional.

A bunch of incompetent, money-grubbing people, starting with the receptionist who answers the calls and thinks she's talking to a friend... What an incompetent and rude woman! I brought my lovebird in because of his eyes; he couldn't see and one eye was bad. I brought him here as an emergency because my vet is on vacation... (I don't know what an emergency is when they give you appointments for everything...) He already has a diagnosed case of intestinal candidiasis... I started explaining the whole process, bursting into tears, and all the guy did was recite the entire price list for all the tests. Without any empathy whatsoever, when they're unnecessary. (It's like if I went to the doctor because my eyes hurt, and they ran tests on everything except my eyes.) And I repeat, I took him because his eye is in bad shape and he can't see. The bird eats, drinks, and everything seems fine. X-ray, blood work, stool test, medication, consultation, etc. 250 euros.
And then they tell me his eye is in very bad shape, and that in a week, if there's an opening, or maybe tomorrow, the ophthalmologist will see me? And just to tell me if he's going blind or not? Another 100 euros for the consultation? And when did you send me eye drops on the very first day? On top of all this, they send me the prescription for candidiasis, I go to the pharmacy and they tell me that prescription doesn't exist in oral form? Only injectable? And how could a veterinarian not know that? Honestly, it's not very professional... I called the girl to tell her this, and she insisted the prescription existed... The only thing is they have to make me another one because they have to change a number... Anyway... On top of all this, I had an appointment with the ophthalmologist the next day at 8:00 PM. I spoke with the girl at 12:30 AM, and I assumed that since I had to go to the appointment that afternoon, they would give it to me then, but no, because the girl told me she would send me the prescription earlier to speed things up since that prescription takes more than a week and my bird is sick... (They give them...) (SAME) DO YOU THINK SHE SENT ME THE RECIPE ALL DAY? No, but yes, at 10 in the morning I did have a missed call and a WhatsApp message reminding me of my ophthalmologist appointment... so that shows how much they care about animals... And lastly, after waiting all day for my bird's prescription, writing and calling me to scold me for not going to the appointment, when I told her I'd been waiting all day for a prescription too and I'm still here, well, the woman is here getting defensive, in a very unprofessional way, telling me that the day hasn't I'D FINISHED, THAT WAS THE VET WHO HAD TO SEND IT, AND I WAS SILENT TO SEE IF I SHOULD GO TO THE APPOINTMENT OR NOT...? AFTER THAT I TOLD HER THAT THEY ONLY CARE ABOUT MONEY INSTEAD OF THE ANIMALS AND THE SHAMELESS WOMAN HANGED UP ON ME...

DON'T BRING YOUR ANIMALS HERE, THEY ONLY CARE ABOUT MONEY.

I took my lovebird to the emergency vet in October, and they treated us wonderfully. The same was true at subsequent appointments. I was so happy to have finally found a clinic I could trust for lovebirds. But one day, they returned my lovebird to me in terrible condition. I'd never seen him like that, and it was supposed to be a simple check-up where everything was already fine. The little guy was perfectly healthy and happy. They kept him under observation because of how badly the vet saw him, and even then, they returned him to me weak, trembling, not eating, and cold. I thought he wasn't going to survive. We kept him close at home for 48 hours, and we managed to save him. I just wanted an explanation of what happened because we can all make mistakes, and they never gave me one. It's a shame; I trusted them. That day, my world almost collapsed.
Thank you, Brenda.

As is natural for anyone who loses a pet that has been with us for years, we feel a mix of emotions ranging from guilt to wanting to pass the misfortune on to others, in this case, to them. They are good professionals and take excellent care of our rabbits with outstanding results. Thank you.
Thank you Esteban

They're awful people. My partner went there because we'd found an injured pigeon, and the receptionist told him that if he didn't pay, she wouldn't help it and that he should just let it die. She said they charge like any other business. That alone makes you wonder about someone who doesn't care about an animal's life. That's no way to respond; I find it shameful. I hope no one takes their animals there like that. The woman is rude and unpleasant. I told her to watch out for the pigeon, and I hope she manages to save the poor thing.
We are very grateful for your attention; you attended to an emergency last night and saved our goat, recommending fast-acting activated charcoal. Thank you so much.

A few months ago, I took my hamster to the vet. First of all, I have no complaints about their veterinary knowledge; they correctly diagnosed and prescribed the treatment for my pet. However, their lack of compassion left much to be desired. They recommended surgery for a possible pyometra that hadn't yet developed, knowing that my hamster had a heart condition and might not survive the operation (besides the fact that he was an older hamster). I changed vets, and they completely advised against the surgery, as it wouldn't extend his life and would be an unnecessary expense for me.

I'm not denying that they are good veterinarians, but I don't think they are empathetic with their patients; instead, they seem focused on getting more money out of you. No other vet has ever charged me €30 for a 5-minute checkup like this one did.
Makes money

Hello, Pablo. We're sorry to see your one-star rating. We couldn't find you in our database using the name in the review, so we can't identify what happened.

If you had a negative experience with us, we would appreciate it if you could tell us why. It's important for us to review your feedback, and it also helps other users understand the context of the rating.

When a negative review doesn't include any comments and we can't link it to any specific customer, it's difficult to know if it actually reflects an experience at our hospital or if it might be a mistaken review.
Their entire team is made up of true professionals. I rescued a lovebird, and they were wonderful people, not people who charge exorbitant prices by taking advantage of any situation.

I'm writing to clarify the response you gave to Sartan (Soledad Lambea Gonzalo) regarding Nina the Wood Pigeon. I'm Anabel de Mena; the registration was done in my name, but you have Sole's name on file since she made the transfer.
When I arrived, they did tell me I could take her to a recovery center. I know Grefa and we've taken fledglings, magpies, and swifts there, but I don't have a car right now, and with a pigeon that had a ruptured crop and couldn't fly (the X-ray showed a coracoid rupture), we couldn't wait to find someone who could drive us because time is crucial.
The veterinarian who treated us, Patricia, was incredibly careful and empathetic and did everything she could to help us. I have no problem with her actions; in fact, I'm grateful to her because she closed the rupture so she could survive until the surgery. What I don't understand is the timing. I understand it was Friday and that on weekends, surgery isn't performed unless it's an emergency. We don't have €750 to do it; there was an opening for the operation on Wednesday, five days later.
On Monday at exactly 11:03 a.m., I called because Nina had expelled a worm about 13 cm long during the night (I've attached the photo we took to show them what it looked like). We wanted to take her in to be examined because she didn't look well, to get her dewormed, and to try to move up her follow-up appointment, which was on Tuesday at 2 p.m. The woman who answered the phone, whose name I don't know, told me they would see her on Tuesday and that it was fine. I was left with the feeling that she couldn't be like that, and that afternoon when we went to feed her, she had died.

I blame myself for not taking her somewhere else that Monday, because if they're going to charge me for another emergency visit, I'd rather go to a different vet. I don't know why you say the professionals are working at 9:00 PM. I'm working at 9:30 PM, but you're a 24-hour center. I don't mean to be rude, but if it's a 24-hour center, it's understood that 24-hour coverage is provided. I think your comment was unnecessary since no one doubts that the professionals are working their shifts.

In any case, my thanks to Patricia and my disappointment with the center. It was recommended to me, but I refuse to recommend it.
If the problem is the high volume of surgeries, perhaps a solution should be found so that an animal doesn't have to die waiting for an operation, or if we call because the animal has a new problem, it shouldn't be ignored.
I work at an animal shelter and manage colonies. The truth is, I've never encountered this situation with other animals, so my feeling is the same as Sole's: that pigeons or street birds don't seem to matter as much.

The review isn't negative, as you say:

"solely because of the charge for emergency veterinary care." We gladly paid for the emergency veterinary care, including the x-ray and everything else she needed. The problem is the high cost of the surgery, given that it was an emergency and we couldn't afford it. But that's just how pricing works, and we can't do anything about it except complain about the high price (which I believe I have the right to do). The review is negative because we feel she didn't receive the care she needed when she needed it, and that I called as the veterinarian, Patricia, told me to, but it didn't help at all.

I hope I've been able to clarify the situation we experienced with Nina. I'm left with the frustration that she could be alive if her surgery had been earlier (for example, Monday instead of Wednesday) or if I had been able to take her in on Monday when I called.

Thank you for your response. My review isn't negative, as I already told you on the phone, because of the prices. You deleted it, rewrote it, and posted a third response to my own review. I hope this is now settled.

I read a review that said if they tell you the prognosis is guarded, run!
You replied that the important thing is, if you perceive the case to be serious, to go to the vet immediately because time is crucial for assessment. Well, four days ago we found a young wood pigeon that seemed badly injured. We took it home and, upon checking for possible wounds, saw that its crop was broken in two places. We immediately took it to see if they could do anything for it. There, the first thing they told us was that it was an emergency and would cost €175. It was a Friday, but of course, we went without an appointment. They were following their protocols, right? I knew they would surely have to operate, but if it was done as an emergency, it would cost €750 for the surgery alone, and if we did it on the first day they had available, it would be €200. I must say that the vet who saw us was very polite, and I suppose she was just following company orders. Unfortunately, my situation doesn't allow me to spend a thousand euros on an emergency operation; I wish I could. In the end, they stapled her crop shut, and it didn't look good, but hey, I'm not a vet. That said, two rabbit emergencies came in, and our pigeon was relegated to second place. They sent us home with anti-inflammatories and antibiotics, and in case she wasn't eating, a recovery formula to give through a feeding tube, which is what we've been doing until today when the pigeon passed away. I understand that for many people, pigeons aren't creatures that deserve even a glance, and that the treatment generally given in clinics to stray birds isn't the same as for a bred one; at least that's been my experience.
Part of the blame is mine for believing that the poor thing could hold out until Tuesday, when she had a check-up, and that she was scheduled for surgery on Wednesday. My complaint is the lack of humanity of these companies, or the lack of surgeons, and the fact that they can't operate on an animal the same day or the next, an animal that, as it turned out, was already doomed. I would be grateful if you could offer some kind of payment plan, so that those of us who find injured animals in the street can truly save their lives. It surprises me more and more each time people walk by when they see an injured animal, and if it's a pigeon, well, that's another story. I spent €241 on that consultation, naively thinking that with another €200 I could save her. Life and death aren't always a matter of money. In this case, they were! My name is Soledad Lambea, and the pigeon's name was Nina.
